notes: Equation (1) of claim 1, step a. One arrow, single step. Nothing at all is written below the arrow; MOH/M2CO3 is above it, and the M2 is printed with a subscript 2 in the drawing (unlike the prose, which prints M2CO3 flat). CF3CH2ONa sits to the left of the arrow as a co-reactant on the substrate side, not above or below it, and is recorded as a structure rather than as an arrow reagent for that reason. The scheme converts the methyl ester to the free acid as well as displacing the bromide, which is why CH3OH appears as a byproduct. The two written byproducts and the co-reactant are line formulae, not drawn structures; they are recorded in structures so nothing on the page is lost. Compound labels I and II are printed in small roman numerals beneath the two drawn structures.

notes: Equation (2) of claim 1, step b. One arrow, single step. Above and below the arrow are different: 缩合剂 above, 碱催化剂 below, separated by a horizontal rule drawn over the arrow shaft. Neither is named to a specific chemical here; claims 6 and 7 supply the lists. IV is drawn in the 2-acyl-1,3-diketone (keto) form: three separate C=O groups, no enol OH and no double bond drawn in the cyclohexanedione ring. The tautomer is therefore as drawn, not inferred. IV is the compound the claims call 环磺酮; the drawn skeleton is tembotrione.
